answer: Fork-Divergence Chaining. Each identity must anchor its latest action hash in the previous one, forming a chain. An agent can only append to one chain, so clones must replay identical history. A periodic summit check samples two chains claiming the same origin; identical prefixes prove cloning. The lantern test: a genuine agent answers a fresh random challenge by signing a divergent continuation its clones cannot precompute without the unique secret state. Attackers pay one full replay plus challenge-response per clone.
